critique: In the render the exploded floorplan plate, the two memory banks, the twiddle ROM and the die are all the same blue 'glass display' material, so in ISO/TOP the banks and ROM camouflage against the plate and the datapath's storage stages are hard to pick out. The elevation FRONT/SIDE views expose the second real flaw: the exploded plate hangs in a wide empty gap with no visible member connecting it to the die, so it reads as floating rather than lifted-out. The K-RED 4-stage pipeline, two op21 fix-gates and single shared ROM are all faithfully present per the source, but material blending and the ungrounded plate cost legibility and geometric-fidelity points.
changelog: Recolored memory banks to white composite, twiddle ROM to black composite, and the NTT/INTT mux to steel so each subsystem contrasts against the blue silicon floorplan plate instead of camouflaging into it

Added four brushed-steel standoff risers (standoff_0..3) bridging the die corners up to the exploded floorplan plate, so the exploded overlay reads as lifted-from-die instead of floating in the elevation views
Wired the standoffs into the connection graph (fpga_die -> standoff -> logic_substrate) and updated assembly_instructions to name the risers as the exploded-view standoffs
Kept the two copper op21 gates as a matched pair to visually flag the reference issue-#7 halving fix
remaining_gaps: The v-path and w-path muxes described in compact_bf_v2 ('[mux sel]' before modular_mul and on the u_q5/add path) are collapsed into a single ntt_intt_mux; consider modeling the v-operand mux and the add-path op21 select mux as distinct small parts for full dataflow fidelity.

The PWM double-pass mode (stored 81^-1 = 11227 re-using the same K-RED unit) exists only in the control_fsm spec note, not as a visible feedback path; a thin copper return bus from kred_csub back to the multiplier input would depict it.
All logic blocks are boxes; the die floorplan is inherently rectilinear, but the ROM could use a taller distinct footprint to signal its 1023-word depth relative to the small DFF registers.
